interest: Standard-Vacuum manager finds Japanese living conditions resilient under 1941 rationing.
overview: C. E. Meyer's 1941 letter finds Japan's living conditions little changed, food scarce but people surprisingly well clothed despite rationing.

people.name: C. E. Meyer
people.role: Manager of the Standard-Vacuum Company in Japan

subfiles.about: An excerpt from a letter by Standard-Vacuum manager C. E. Meyer assessing domestic living conditions, food supply, and consumer goods rationing in Japan in early 1941.
subfiles.from: C. E. Meyer (Manager, Standard-Vacuum Company in Japan)
subfiles.summary: C. E. Meyer of Standard-Vacuum reports Japan's living conditions little changed after a year's absence: bread, potatoes, lamb, and game scarce, breadline grumbling mild, and the populace surprisingly well dressed and shod despite three years of wool, cotton, leather, and rubber controls.
subfiles.title: Excerpt from letter of C. E. Meyer on living conditions in Japan
